title: The strange buoyancy of ice
text: Unlike most substances, water is denser {{1}} a liquid than it is as a solid, {{2}} is why ice floats {{3}} top of a frozen lake. The explanation lies {{4}} hydrogen bonding: as water cools towards freezing, its molecules link into a rigid but open lattice, {{5}} holds them unusually far apart. Ice is therefore about nine per cent lighter than an equal volume of water, {{6}} is why icebergs ride so low in the sea. The consequences reach far beyond the laboratory: the water beneath a lid of ice is protected {{7}} the insulating layer above, and every lake that freezes over develops a stable world of its {{8}}, in which fish wait out the winter in comfort.

gaps.explanation: 'As a liquid' pairs with 'as a solid' in the comparison.
Sentential relative after the comma; 'that' cannot start a non-defining clause.
The fixed phrase is 'on top of'.
'Lie in' — the cause is located in the bonding.
Non-defining relative after the comma: which holds them.

gaps.hint: relative: ___, __ is why icebergs ride low
gaps.explanation: Another sentential relative summing up the previous clause.
Passive agent: the layer is what protects, so 'by' introduces it.
'Of its own' — the emphatic possessive phrase.
